age.evidence: Mice were 5-7 months of age at the time the experiments were performed.

sex.evidence: In total, 55 male mice (27 WT and 28 KO) and 36 female mice were used (13 WT and 23 KO).

dosing.evidence: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg), provided by Usona Institute Inc., was dissolved in 0.9% saline solution, and administered via intraperitoneal (i.p.) injection.

handling.evidence: Paper does not describe a handling protocol.

group_housing.evidence: Mice were housed in groups of 2-5 same sex/genotype mice in individually ventilated cages.

day_night_flipped.evidence: 12:12 light/dark cycle (lights were on from 7am to 7pm). All behavioural testing was conducted during the light cycle (9 a.m.-4 p.m.).

enrichment_housing.evidence: Paper does not mention home-cage enrichment items.

assays.assay_description: Distance travelled measured in a 26 × 26 × 38 cm photo-beam activity chamber (Coulbourn) for 15 min before and 60 min after acute psilocybin/saline injection; analysed in 5-min bins.

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were acclimatised to their environment for at least 30 min before testing

setup_restrain.evidence: placing mice in a 26 cm × 26 cm × 38 cm photo-beam activity chamber

food_restriction.evidence: Test conducted in photo-beam chamber with no food present.

water_restriction.evidence: Test conducted in photo-beam chamber with no water present.

time_to_assay.evidence: Locomotor activity was measured for 15 min before and 60 min after acute psilocybin administration.

sample_size.evidence: n = 11-14 mice per group (males); n = 6-11 mice per group (females).

outcomes.summary: Acute 1 mg/kg psilocybin increased total distance travelled over 60 min in WT mice but not in SAPAP3 KO mice. In males, psilocybin increased locomotion vs saline at 10, 30, 40 and 55 min; in females, the effect was significant in WT but not in KO mice.
outcomes.statistics: Genotype × treatment interaction F(1,83)=9.502, p=0.003; WT psilocybin vs saline p<0.0001, KO p=0.772; males time × treatment F(12,588)=4.37, p<0.0001; females time × genotype × treatment F(12,384)=2.32, p=0.007.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin increased the distance travelled for WT (p < 0.0001) but not KO (p = 0.772) mice compared to saline administration

B1_num_measures.evidence: we analysed distance travelled (cm) via 5-min bins

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: distance travelled analysed via 5-min bins across the session

B4_ethological.evidence: Locomotor distance is not an ethological behaviour.

B5_social.evidence: Animals tested alone in the chamber.

D1_continuity.evidence: Recorded 15 min before and 60 min after injection on the same day in one continuous bout.

D3_recording_days.evidence: Locomotor data collected on a single day.

D4_baseline.evidence: We used the 10-15-min bin before injection as our baseline (time point 0).

D5_followup.evidence: No locomotor recording ≥24 h after dosing.

assays.assay_description: In the 15 min immediately after injection, mice were placed in the locomotor cell and video-recorded from above (1920×1088, 25 fps); head-twitches manually scored by a blinded researcher and binned at 5, 10 and 15 min.

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were acclimatised to their environment for at least 30 min before testing

setup_restrain.evidence: mice were placed in the locomotor cell and were video recorded from a top view

food_restriction.evidence: No food present in chamber during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water present in chamber during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: In the 15 min immediately after injection

sample_size.evidence: n = 12-15 mice per group (males); n = 6-12 mice per group (females).

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg) significantly increased head-twitches at 5, 10 and 15 min after injection in both WT and KO mice of both sexes. SAPAP3 KO mice exhibited significantly more head-twitches than WT mice overall.
outcomes.statistics: Males: time × treatment F(2,102)=8.16, p<0.001; females: time × treatment F(2,64)=3.80, p=0.028; genotype effect F(1,83)=7.168, p=0.009.
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly increased the number of head twitches compared to saline (p < 0.0001). SAPAP3 KO animals had a greater number of head twitches compared to WT animals (p = 0.009).

B1_num_measures.evidence: The HTR (head-twitch count) was the measured variable.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Head twitches scored in 5-min bins (5, 10, 15 min after injection).

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours by the rubric.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: The behaviour was manually scored by a blinded and trained researcher.

D2_session_duration.evidence: In the 15 min immediately after injection

assays.assay_description: 26 × 26 × 38 cm photo-beam arena divided into light (750 lux) and dark compartments; mice placed in the dark side and allowed to explore for 10 min; % time in light, distance travelled and number of transitions recorded at baseline, 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days post-injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: mice were acclimatised to their environment for at least 30 min before testing

setup_restrain.evidence: allowed to explore the arena for 10 min

time_to_assay.evidence: assessed at four time-points (i.e., baseline, 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days after acute psilocybin injection)

sample_size.evidence: n = 12-15 mice per group (males); n = 6-12 mice per group (females).

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin did not alter anxiety-like behaviour in the LDB: no effect on % time in the light, distance travelled, or number of transitions in either sex or genotype, at any post-treatment timepoint. KO mice showed reduced light-side time, distance, and transitions vs WT regardless of treatment.
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin administration did not alter light duration (F1,50 = 1.47; p = 0.231) and light duration did not vary over time

B1_num_measures.evidence: percentage of time spent in the light compartment ... distance travelled and the number of transitions

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone preference and locomotion are spatial measures, not ethological behaviours.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate avoidance test, no learning required.

E2_shelter.evidence: fully enclosed dark compartment by choice

E6_spatial.evidence: divided into light and dark compartments with a black Plexiglas insert

D1_continuity.evidence: assessed at four time-points (baseline, 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days)

D2_session_duration.evidence: allowed to explore the arena for 10 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Four recording days: baseline, 24 h, 72 h, 8 days.

D4_baseline.evidence: Based on the light-dark box and grooming baseline measurements (1 week prior to drug administration)

D5_followup.evidence: Recordings at 24 h, 72 h and 8 days post-injection.

assays.assay_description: Mice individually placed in a 30 × 16 × 20 cm rectangular tank and video-recorded for 20 min; the last 10 min were scored manually with BORIS for percentage grooming time, grooming bouts (>4 s) and interrupted bouts at baseline, 24 h, 72 h and 8 days post-injection.

setup_habituation.evidence: transferred to the grooming behavioural room (in their home cage) and habituated for 30 min before grooming was assessed

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were individually placed in a rectangular fish tank ... and recorded with a video camera for 20 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food in tank during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: No water in tank during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: Grooming behaviours were assessed at four timepoints (i.e., baseline, 24 h, 72 h and 8 days after psilocybin)

sample_size.evidence: n = 12-15 mice per group (males); n = 6-12 mice per group (females).

outcomes.summary: Acute 1 mg/kg psilocybin reduced grooming duration in male SAPAP3 KO mice at 3 and 8 days post-injection (no effect in WT males), and reduced grooming in both WT and KO female mice across timepoints. Number of grooming bouts was not altered. In males, head-twitch number was negatively correlated with grooming duration (R²=0.24, p=0.007).
outcomes.statistics: Males: genotype F(1,51)=89.91, p<0.0001; time × treatment × genotype F(2,102)=4.58, p=0.012; KO-PSIL vs KO-SAL: day 3 p=0.010, day 8 p=0.016. Females: genotype F(1,32)=12.50, p=0.001; treatment F(1,32)=4.99, p=0.033.
outcomes.evidence: KO mice that received psilocybin had reduced grooming duration compared to KO mice that received saline at 3 (p = 0.010) and 8 days (p = 0.016) after injection ... Psilocybin reduced grooming in both KO and WT mice (F1,32 = 4.99; p = 0.033)

B1_num_measures.evidence: Percentage grooming time, grooming bouts, and interrupted bouts were quantified.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Grooming behaviour was assessed from the last 10 min; no within-session time-bin analysis.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: An interrupted bout was calculated when a mouse had stopped grooming for a period of <4 s, and then continued grooming.

B4_ethological.evidence: Grooming or scratching of face, body, genitals, and tail was quantified — a natural ethological behaviour.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: A trained blinded observer manually scored and time-stamped grooming behaviour via BORIS.

E1_environment_type.evidence: rectangular fish tank (30 cm × 16 cm × 20 cm)

D1_continuity.evidence: Grooming assessed at baseline, 24 h, 72 h and 8 days after psilocybin.

D2_session_duration.evidence: recorded with a video camera for 20 min

D3_recording_days.evidence: Four recording days: baseline, 24 h, 72 h, 8 days.

D4_baseline.evidence: grooming baseline measurements (1 week prior to drug administration)

D5_followup.evidence: Recordings at 24 h, 72 h and 8 days post-injection.

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed on the four assays: Locomotor Activity, HTR, LDB, Grooming — kept as distinct paradigms.
B1 for Locomotor Activity scored 0 ('1' measure: distance travelled only); glm's score=1 with value '1' was a clerical inconsistency.

B1 for HTR scored 0 ('1' measure: head-twitch count); gptoss treated different timepoints as separate measures, which conflicts with the rubric (timepoints = temporal dynamics, not separate measures).
B3 for Grooming scored 1 because interrupted-bout analysis captures bout microstructure, consistent with gptoss; qwen and glm missed this.
E2 for LDB scored 1 (fully enclosed dark compartment counts as shelter per rubric: 'dark compartment in light-dark box (fully enclosed)'); overrode gptoss's score=0.
time_to_assay set to 'multiple' for LDB and Grooming since they were tested at baseline, 24 h, 72 h, and 8 days post-injection.
sex_dependent for Grooming set to 'yes' per the paper's explicit sex × treatment interaction and the separate male/female analyses.
